messages:
jamal: Heads-up — we have the release next Tue 09:00 UTC. I want to coordinate a staggered TF apply for the networking + IAM changes. This touches cross-account trust and a couple of service roles.

maria: +1. can you paste the plan? especially worried about iam_role_policy_attachment changes.

kevin: quick note — pin provider to avoid recent provider+TF drift. I recommend aws provider v5.2.0 for this apply. adds 0 risk.

jamal: agree on pin. I'll update modules/providers.tf to `version = "~> 5.2.0"` and push a commit to the release branch.

infra-qa: pasted plan excerpt:
```
# aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.prod_lambda_attach will be updated in-place
~ resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "prod_lambda_attach" {
    role       = "lambda-prod-exec" -> "lambda-prod-exec"
    policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::1234567890:policy/AllowX" -> "arn:aws:iam::1234567890:policy/AllowY"
}
```

infra-qa: also: backend state remote lock ok, no drift detected in tfstate.

maria: :eyes: Will the policy change break any running jobs? looks like the new policy tightens S3 access. can we canary apply to staging VPC first?

rachael: Suggestion: staggered rollout plan 
- step A: apply to staging/us-west1 (10:00 UTC)
- step B: monitor 30m, smoke tests run by QA
- step C: apply to prod/us-west1 (11:00 UTC)
- step D: if OK, apply rest of regions

kevin: sounds good. add a preflight check to ensure no active long-running ECS deployments that depend on the old policy.

jamal: scheduling change window: Tue 09:00–12:00 UTC. tagging required approvers @maria @kevin @sre-oncall for manual thumbs. please react with :white_check_mark: or :x:.

maria: :white_check_mark:

kevin: :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: :white_check_mark: — oncall will watch logs and auto-escalate if latency or auth errors spike.

deploy-bot: preflight-check OK — remote state locked, provider version pinned to 5.2.0, modules validated. Next: manual approve to run `terraform apply` in `infra/networking` workspace.

jamal: giving manual approve to start canary at 10:00 UTC in us-west1. infra-qa, please standby for smoke harness.

infra-qa: ready. smoke tests: s3 read/write, lambda invoke, ecs task start.

(10:00 UTC) deploy-bot: starting terraform apply on infra/networking (workspace=us-west1-canary) — initiating plan/apply.

(10:02 UTC) deploy-bot: apply in-progress... resources being updated.

(10:05 UTC) deploy-bot: apply failed: error updating aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.prod_lambda_attach -> "Invalid principal in policy"

kevin: oh. that looks like a cross-account principal ARN is malformed or the target account hasn't accepted the trust. did we update the principal to a role in account 0987654321?

maria: checking account trust logs... yep, the target account API indicates the role doesn't exist yet — the role creation in the other repo didn't go out due to a pipeline issue.

jamal: rollback plan: restore previous policy via `terraform apply -target=aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.prod_lambda_attach` rollback commit (revert PR queued).

deploy-bot: running rollback apply (target=aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.prod_lambda_attach) — starting.

(10:12 UTC) deploy-bot: rollback apply succeeded. state restored and remote lock released.

sre-oncall: Verified no auth spikes in the last 15m. Good catch. Recommend gating any further runs until cross-account role exists.

rachael: moving to postmortem action items: 
- coordinate cross-repo change (create role) and merge order
- add a preflight script to verify existence of external principals
- update runbook with immediate rollback commands and who to call

jamal: I'll open the follow-up Jira, link to the role PR, and schedule the retry in next release slot. thanks all.

kevin: can we add an automated check in the CI that queries the target account IAM for principal existence before terraform plan? that would have prevented this.

infra-qa: adding test to smoke harness: verify principals for IAM attachments.

jamal: final — re-scheduled canary for Wed 09:30 UTC after dependent role PR is merged. marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
